short_description: Insulin-secreting endocrine cell of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans: a rounded polygonal cell whose TEM signature is its thousands of insulin secretory granules — each a membrane-bound vesicle holding a dense, often angular crystalline zinc-insulin core inside a clear pale halo. It senses blood glucose through its own metabolism and releases the granules by exocytosis toward an adjacent fenestrated capillary, in pulses.
color_legend: cell body warm translucent sand/amber (colour is teaching convention — the living cell is colourless), insulin granules: thin teal membrane ring around a clear pale-ivory halo with a deep indigo-violet angular crystalline core, nucleus soft lavender-violet sphere, Golgi apparatus dusty apricot-orange stack of curved cisternae, rough ER sage-green ribbon cisternae studded with dark ribosome dots, mitochondria muted orange-red ovals, fenestrated capillary soft rose-red vessel running along one edge with a thin porous wall, background neutral dark charcoal (textbook/3d) or warm aged paper (watercolor)
